pairs_diagnostics.cointegration_status_note: Formation spread shows marginal stationarity evidence at the 10% level (Engle-Granger p = 0.0994, ADF t = -3.04, return correlation = 0.84).

parameter_surface.methodology_note: Evaluated K=25 parameter combinations across Entry Z-Score Threshold (σ) and Spread Z-Score Window (Days). Per Bailey & López de Prado (2014), the expected maximum Sharpe Ratio under a null hypothesis of zero skill across K=25 trials is 0.37. Inspect whether performance forms a broad plateau across neighbouring parameters or is isolated to a single spike.

methodology_notes: Causal Signal & Execution Timing: Signals are evaluated strictly at the close of bar t using data [0..t] and executed at bar t+1 (next_open) with 5.0 bps commission + 5.0 bps adverse slippage per leg.

Chronological Holdout Separation: Dataset (2011 trading days) is partitioned into an In-Sample Formation split (2018-01-02 to 2021-12-29, 1006 days) and a Held-Out Out-of-Sample split (2021-12-30 to 2025-12-31, 1005 days).

Inference under Non-Normality & Serial Dependence: Sharpe Ratio standard errors and Probabilistic Sharpe Ratios (PSR) incorporate sample skewness and kurtosis per Mertens (2002) and Lo (2002). Confidence intervals use the Politis & Romano (1994) Stationary Bootstrap, and benchmark alpha/beta t-statistics use Newey-West (1987) HAC standard errors.

Pairs Cointegration Formation: OLS hedge ratio (beta = 1.5366, alpha = -2.8923) and Engle-Granger / ADF cointegration tests were estimated exclusively on the Formation split (2018-01-02 to 2021-12-29) and held frozen during Out-of-Sample evaluation.
limitations: Historical Simulation Boundary: Historical backtests and statistical significance measures describe past price paths and do not guarantee future market behaviour or liquidity.

Execution & Microstructure Simplification: Fills are modelled at daily Open/Close bars with fixed basis-point slippage and do not model intraday limit-order-book queue priority, borrow fee spikes on short legs, or market impact for large notional orders.

Selection & Multiple-Testing Bias: Inspecting multiple thresholds or re-running hypotheses on the same dataset increases false-discovery probability; consult the Bailey & López de Prado (2014) Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR) and Out-of-Sample split metrics when interpreting results.
